newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian 1995/96 coffee crop put at 12.9 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: Colombian 1995/96 coffee crop put at 12.9 mln bags.

text.p: Colombia produced about 12.9 million 60-kilo bags of coffee in the 1995-96 coffee year, according to Jorge Cardenas, head of the National Federation of Coffee Growers.

Cardenas stressed that the 12.9 million figure was only a "very preliminary" estimate, however, and that it could be weeks before the federation releases any official production numbers for the coffee year that ended last month.

In remarks to reporters, Cardenas also said that coffee shipments to Colombia's ports had returned to normal Friday morning, after an 11-day truckers' strike that had paralyzed key sectors of the economy ended late Thursday.

He said delays could still be expected in Colombia's October coffee shipments, however, and that about 150,000 60-kilo bags promised for delivery this month were unlikely to reach roasters until November.
Private exporters say enormous backlogs have built up in Colombia's ports since the strike began at midnight, October 13, and it will take days or even weeks before shipments return to normal.
Industry sources had said previously that production in the 1995/96 coffee year was expected to total no more than about 12.6 million 60-kilo bags, down from 13 million in the previous coffee year.
